OLD BUSINESS

Member Huhn moved to approve the minutes of October 20, 2026. Seconded by Member Brush. Roll call vote

NEW BUSINESS 
1. Zone Change –  56 Godsoe Road – Map-Lot R28 -003-A – Industry and Service 
District (I&S) to Urban Industry District (UID) – To amend the Land Development Code 
by changing the lot located at 56 Godsoe  Road from the Industry and Service District 
(I&S) to the Urban Industry District (UID). Said area contains approximately 4.73 acres 
total and is more particularly indicated on the map attached hereto and made part hereof. 
Applicant/Owner: FedEx Freight, Inc.
Page  2 | 5 
 
City of Bangor Planning Division 
Planning Board Meeting Minutes – Tuesday, November 17, 2026 
Chair Boucher introduced the agenda item. 
 
Applicant Representative Patrick Lyons presented on the proposed zone change. He discussed that the 
property is located inside the Growth Boundary and is identified in the future land use map in the 2022 
Comprehensive Plan as an industrial future land use area. Lyons discussed that the change in zone will 
not change the property’s use, but rather allows the site to be used more fully. He noted that the request 
is consistent with the zoning pattern of the area.  
 
Chair Boucher asked for any questions from the Board – there were none.   
 
Chair Boucher opened public comment – there were none. Public comment closed. 
 
Member Brush moved that the Board recommends that the City Council ought to accept a zone change 
for 56 Godsoe Road from Industry and Service District (I&S) to Urban Industry District (UID). Seconded 
by Member Huhn. Roll call vote conducted – all voting members in favor, none opposed. Motion passed. 
 
 
2. Land Development Permit Application – Major Site Development – 32 Thatcher St 
– Map-Lot 017-011 – RH Foster Energy, LLC – Land Development Permit Application 
– Major Site Development for the construction of a 2,000 square foot cold storage 
warehouse at property located at 32 Thatcher Street, Map-Lot 017-011, in the General 
Commercial and Service District (GC&S) and Industry and Service District (I&S). 
Applicant/Owner: Bangor Lewiston Properties LLC. 
Chair Boucher introduced the agenda item. 
 
Chair Boucher noted that there are six Planning Board members in attendance and asked whether the 
applicant would like to postpone review until there are seven Board members in attendance. The 
applicant confirmed the Board may continue with review. 
 
Member Hobson moved that the application was deemed complete on November 17, 2026, all applicable 
fees for the project have been paid, and the proposed project is a major site development. Seconded by 
Member Huhn. Roll call vote conducted – all voting members in favor, none opposed. Motion passed. 
 
Applicant Representative Justine Drake  presented on the project proposal to add cold storage to their 
existing outdoor site. She provided an overview of the proposed site plan and discus sed details 
surrounding lighting, buffers, and grading. 
 
Chair Boucher asked staff for comments or questions – there were none. 
 
Chair Boucher asked about the residential-appearing house contained in the impervious area. Applicant 
Representative Drake clarified that while the use of the building is residential, it is not residentially zoned.  
 
Chair Boucher asked if there is a right of way along the narrow strip that abuts 27 Olive Street – Applicant 
Representative Drake confirmed.
Page  3 | 5 
 
City of Bangor Planning Division 
Planning Board Meeting Minutes – Tuesday, November 17, 2026 
Chair Boucher asked whether there are similar buffer requirements for residential use of a non- zoned 
residential property – Planning Officer Collette responded that the code refers to the residential zone, not 
the use.  
 
Chair Boucher opened public comment – there were none. Public comment closed.  
 
Member Huhn moved that the Board finds that, based on Exhibits 2 and 8, the applicant satisfied Land 
Development Code §165-33.1’s requirements surrounding Erosion and Sediment Control. Seconded by 
Member Hobson. Roll call vote conducted – all voting members in favor, none opposed. Motion passed. 
 
Member Hobson moved that the Board finds that, based on Exhibit 2, the applicant satisfied §165-62 of

requirements for side yard width, §165-65’s requirements for yard space for group buildings, and §165-
68’s requirements of minimum lot frontage. Seconded by Member Whitford. Roll call vote conducted – all 
voting members in favor, none opposed. Motion passed. 
 
Member Huhn moved that the Board finds that, based on Exhibits 2 and 17, the applicant satisfied §165-
66 of the Land Development Code regarding providing a transitional yard for buildings abutting a 
residential district and §165- 67’s requirement of providing adequate screening of outdoor storage.  
Seconded by Member Whitford. Roll call vote conducted –  all voting members in favor, none opposed. 
Motion passed. 
 
Member Hobson moved that t he Board finds that, based on Exhibits 2, 17, 22, and 23, the applicant 
satisfied §165-72 of the Land Development Code regarding the required number of parking spaces, §165-
73’s requirements regarding parking area location and screening, and §165-74’s requirements regarding 
parking area design, construction and maint enance. Seconded by Member Huhn. Roll call vote 
conducted – all voting members in favor, none opposed. Motion passed. 
 
Member Huhn moved that t he Board finds that, based on Exhibit 2, 17,and 23, the applicant satisfied 
Land Development Code §165- 79 requiri ng adequate utility service, including water, electricity, fire 
protection, and provision for stormwater runoff. Seconded by Member Brush. Roll call vote conducted – 
all voting members in favor, none opposed. Motion passed. 
 
Member Hobson moved that the Board finds that, based on Exhibits 2 and 9, the applicant satisfied §165-
81 of the Land Development Code regarding providing adequate lighting and preventing light pollution 
and trespass. Seconded by Member Huhn. Roll call vote conducted – all voting members in favor, none 
opposed. Motion passed. 
 
Member Huhn moved that t he Board finds that, based on Exhibit 2, the applicant satisfied the Land 
Development Code §165- 83 requiring adequate electrical services.  Seconded by Member Brush. Roll 
call vote conducted – all voting members in favor, none opposed. Motion passed. 
 
Member Hobson moved that the Board finds that, based on Exhibits 2, 17, and 23, the applicant satisfied 
the Land Development Code §165- 84 requiring provisions for surface water and storm drainage . 
Seconded by Member Huhn. Roll call vote conducted –  all voting members in favor, none opposed. 
Motion passed.

City of Bangor Planning Division 
Planning Board Meeting Minutes – Tuesday, November 17, 2026 
Vice Chair Jonas moved that the Board finds that, based on the findings made in Part 1 of Section IV of 
this document, the Project meets the requirements of § 165-102B for uses within the General Commercial 
and Service District (GC&S).  Seconded by Member Hobson. Roll call vote conducted –  all voting 
members in favor, none opposed. Motion passed. 
 
Member Huhn moved that the Board finds that, based on the findings made in Part 1 of Section IV of this 
document, the Project meets the requirements of § 165- 103B for uses within the Industry and Service 
District (I&S). Seconded by Member Brush. Roll call vote conducted – all voting members in favor, none 
opposed. Motion passed. 
 
Vice Chair Jonas moved that t he Board finds that, based on Exhibit 2, the applicant satisfied Land 
Development Code §165-114B’s requirement that the proposed parking and loading layout are arranged 
in a reasonable and safe configur ation. Seconded by Member Whitford. Roll call vote conducted –  all 
voting members in favor, none opposed. Motion passed. 
 
Member Hobson moved that t he Board finds that, based on Exhibits 2 and 22, the applicant satisfied 
Land Development Code §165- 114D’s requirements regarding minimizing adverse effects from 
stormwater runoff and ensuring adequate stormwater collection capacity. Seconded by Member Huhn. 
Roll call vote conducted – all voting members in favor, none opposed. Motion passed. 
 
Member Huhn moved that the Board finds that, based on Exhibits 2 and 9, the applicant satisfied Land 
Development Code §165-114E’s requirement of situating and properly screening outdoor storage areas 
and that all outdoor lighting shall be designed, installed, and maintained to avoid adverse effects on 
adjacent properties. Seconded by Member Hobson. Roll call vote conducted – all voting members in 
favor, none opposed. Motion passed. 
 
Member Hobson moved that t he Board finds that, based on Exhibits 2, 17, 22, and 23, the applicant 
satisfied Land Development Code §165 -114F’s requirements for landscaping.  Seconded by Member 
Whitford. Roll call vote conducted – all voting members in favor, none opposed. Motion passed. 
 
Member Huhn moved that t he Board finds that, based on Exhibit 2, the applicant satisfied Land 
Development Code §165-114G’s requirement that the location of the buildings meet all required setbacks 
and are situated to avoid unreasonable adverse effects on adjacent properties or public rights -of-way. 
Seconded by Member Whitford. Roll call vote conducted –  all voting members in favor, none opposed. 
Motion passed. 
 
Vice Chair Jonas moved that t he Board finds that, based on Exhibits 2 and 23, the applicant satisfied 
§165-135 of the Land Development Code regarding height limits, floor area ratio, impervious surface 
ratio, and buffer yards . Seconded by Member Huhn. Roll call vote conducted –  all voting members in 
favor, none opposed. Motion passed. 
Member Huhn moved that the Board finds that the Project meets the requirements for a Land 
Development Permit for a Major Site Development and therefore, the Board grants the Land 
Development Permit for the proposed Project. S econded by Member Brush. Roll call vote conducted –  
all voting members in favor, none opposed. Motion passed.

II. Project Description and Permit Requirements 
 
The Project will consist of construction of a 2,000 sq. ft. cold storage warehouse. The 
Project is located at 32 Thatcher St, Map-Lot 017-011, in the Industry & Service District 
(I&S) and General Commercial and Service District (GC&S).  
 
As a permitted use in the General Commercial and Service District (GC&S) and Industry & 
Service District (I&S), per §165-102 and §165-103, the Project must meet the 
requirements of Article II through XII and any applicable development standards of Article 
XIX. This Project must also meet the Land Development Approval Standards outlined in 
§165-114.

V. Decision 
 
The Board finds that the Project meets the requirements for a Land Development Permit 
for a Major Site Development and therefore, the Board grants the Land Development 
Permit for the proposed Project.  
 
VI. General Permit Requirements: 
 
A. This permit does not relieve the applicant from any other state or federal permits that 
may be required for the project.  
 
B. Prior to construction, the applicant should contact the Code Enforcement Office and 
Engineering Office for any additional permits that may be required. 
 
C. Applicant must commence construction within one year from the date of approval and 
complete the project by November 17, 2028, unless extensions of time are granted per  
the provisions of Chapter 165-113E. 
 
D. No certificate of occupancy  for any structure will be issued by the Code Enforcement 
Division until the property for which the certificate is sought is in compliance with all 
applicable regulations, including but not limited to building, zoning, and stormwater 
requirements. A tempor ary certificate of occupancy may be issued when necessary 
under the provisions of § 165-113G of the City’s Land Development Code. 
 
E. Upon completion, a digital as -built plan or plans shall be submitted to the Code 
Enforcement Officer. Additionally, a certificate of compliance stamped by a registered 
professional engineer or a registered land surveyor must be submitted to the Code 
Enforcement Office indicating that the site development has been completed in 
accordance with the approved revised plan. 
 
Failure to comply with the conditions listed above constitutes a violation of the Bangor Land 
Development Code as prescribed in Chapter 165-10G.

Title, Ordinance 
 
Amending Chapter 165, Land Development Code, District Map to Re-Zone a Portion of the Property Located at 
1397 Ohio Street from Urban Residence 1 (URD-1) and Rural Residence and Agricultural (RR&A) to 
Government and Institutional Service District (G&ISD). 
 
Summary 
 
This ordinance would amend the Land Development Code, District Map to re-zone a portion of the property at 
Map-Lot R14-013, located at 1397 Ohio Street, from Urban Residence 1 (URD-1) and Rural Residence and 
Agricultural (RR&A) to Government and Institutional Service District (G&ISD). The total area requested to be 
changed is approximately 5.42 acres. The applicants and owners of record are Daniel and Heather Smith. 
 
This area is within the growth boundary shown in the 2022 Comprehensive Plan and the future land use map 
in the Plan shows this property in the Neighborhood Residential area, which consists of “medium-density 
residential development with limited commercial and institutional uses that are complementary to the 
surrounding residential land uses”.

CITY COUNCIL ORDINANCE 
Date: November 23, 2026 
Assigned to Councilor:  
 
ORDINANCE, Amending Chapter 165, Land Development Code, District Map to Re-Zone a Portion of the 
Property Located at 1397 Ohio Street from Urban Residence 1 (URD-1) and Rural Residence and Agricultural 
(RR&A) to Government and Institutional Service District (G&ISD). 
 
WHEREAS, the land uses around the property consist primarily residential with some institutional;  
 
WHEREAS, the zoning around the property consists primarily of Rural Residence and Agricultural District 
(RR&A), Government and Institutional Service District (G&ISD), and Urban Residence 1 District (URD-1); 
 
WHEREAS, the 2022 Comprehensive Plan and the future land use map in the Plan shows this property in the 
Neighborhood Residential area, which consists of “medium-density residential development with limited 
commercial and institutional uses that are complementary to the surrounding residential land uses”;  
 
BE IT ORDAINED BY THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF BANGOR AS FOLLOWS, THAT 
 
Chapter 165 of the Code of the City of Bangor, District Map, is amended to reclassify a portion of the property 
at Map-Lot R14-013, located at 1397 Ohio Street, from Urban Residence 1 (URD-1) and Rural Residence and 
Agricultural (RR&A) to Government and Institutional Service District (G&ISD). The total area requested to be 
changed is approximately 5.42 acres and is shown in the attached exhibits.

questions about the process or participation in the hearing process.

ZONE CHANGE PROCESS 
1. Applications for zoning amendment must be filed in the Planning Division Office at City Hall. 
2. A Council Ordinance containing the proposed zoning amendment will be drawn up by the Planning Office 
and placed on the Council Agenda.  
3. A public hearing must be scheduled to be held by the Planning Board on the proposed amendment (the 
City Council can take no action until after the Planning Board hearing and report).  
4. A notice of the public hearing must be placed in a newspaper at least 14 days prior to the hearing. A 
Notice must be mailed to owners of abutting property within 100 feet of the property subject to rezoning 
action.  
5. Recommendations to the City Council must  be approved by a majority of all members of the Board 
present and voting. 
6. After receipt of the Planning Board recommendation the City Council must act on the zone change 
request (however, a proposed amendment which has been not recommended by the Planning Board 
may only be enacted by a 2/3 vote of the City Council). 
 
Only the City Council can change zoning, as it is an ordinance amendment. 
 
ABOUT THIS PROPOSED CHANGE 
CURRENT PROPERTY ZONE: Rural Residence and Agricultural District (RR&A) - § 165-105 
• Allowed Uses 
o Agriculture. 
o The sale of farm, nursery, dairy or poultry products within a structure having a gross floor area of not 
more than 500 square feet. 
o Sale of farm products where: 
 The retail area shall not exceed 2,500 square feet. 
 The property is located on a major arterial street. 
 The property is a working farm. 
o One-family dwellings, with additional dwelling units permitted given the following: 
 If the lot is inside the Growth Boundary defined in the City's most recently adopted 
Comprehensive Plan: 
• If no dwelling exists on a lot, up to four units are allowed, either detached or 
attached. 
• If one dwelling unit exists on the lot, up to two additional units are allowed, one being 
attached to or within the primary dwelling and one being detached. 
• If two dwelling units exist on a lot, no additional units are allowed. 
 If the lot is outside the Growth Boundary defined in the City's most recently adopted 
Comprehensive Plan: 
• If no dwelling exists on a lot, up to two units are allowed, either detached or attached. 
• If one dwelling unit exists on the lot, up to two additional units are allowed, one being 
attached to or within the existing dwelling and one being detached. 
• If two dwelling units exist on a lot, no additional units are allowed. 
 If dwelling units are demolished after the date this section is adopted and the demolition 
results in an empty lot, there can be no increase in the number of units above what existed 
on the lot prior to demolition. 
o Home occupation or profession (subject to the requirements of Article IV). 
o Municipal uses. 
o Minor essential service facilities, under the conditions required by § 165-80.3. 
o Major essential service facilities.
o Community living arrangements, in accordance with 30-A M.R.S.A. § 4357-A, as may be amended. 
o Cluster subdivision for detached single-family dwellings, provided that: 
o Such project has a minimum of five acres. 
o Provision is made for the maintenance in perpetuity of open space areas in such a project. 
o Such project receives approval under Article XVI of this chapter. 
o Cellular telecommunication towers, provided that: 
 They do not exceed 195 feet in height, or the minimum height required under federal law, 
whichever is greater. 
 They are set back from property lines a minimum of 100% of the tower height. 
 They conform to the requirements of § 165-80.1. 
o Bed-and-breakfasts, provided that: 
 Meals provided are limited to patrons and their guests. 
 It is limited to a maximum of 10 guest rooms. 
 It provides, at a minimum, an A Buffer Yard or an equivalent of existing woody vegetation to 
buffer neighboring properties. 
 The applicant demonstrates compliance with the State Plumbing Code for the proposed 
number of units. 
o Small landscaping services business, provided that: 
 The landscaping services use is accessory to the primary use of the parcel as a residence. 
 Facilities, equipment, and storage areas are located at least 50 feet from the property line of 
any other parcel. 
 At least 50 feet of existing or planted woody vegetation creating an effective visual barrier 
must be provided between facilities, equipment and storage areas and the property line of 
any adjacent parcel. 
 No more than four people, including the owner, may be employed or used as independent 
contractors by the landscaping services business. 
 A stockade fence at least six feet in height must enclose any storage or parking area on any 
side not facing a building on the parcel or a street adjacent to the parcel. 
o Small day-care center, provided that it is operated at a dwelling by a resident or residents of the 
dwelling. 
o Accessory dwelling units, under the conditions required by § 165-31.2. 
o Tiny home park, provided that: 
 The site is located within the growth area delineated in the most recently adopted 
Comprehensive Plan. 
 The park meets the requirements of Article XX. 
o Manufactured home parks, provided that: 
 The site is located within the growth area delineated in the most recently adopted 
Comprehensive Plan 
 The park meets the requirements of Article XVII. 
o Hosted and non-hosted short-term rentals (subject to licensing requirements in Chapter 254). 
o Accessory uses on the same lot and customarily incidental to and subordinate to the above uses 
and any use approved under subsection below. 
• Conditional Uses 
o Excavations of soil or loam, provided that they meet the requirements of Article VI. 
o Animal pounds, kennels, animal hospitals, animal clinics, and animal crematoria, provided that 
such facilities are located at least 100 feet from any residential district and at least 150 feet from 
any residential building on an adjoining parcel. 
o Tenting and camping areas, golf courses and driving ranges (except miniature golf courses), 
provided that: 
 They are located on the following arterial highways: Route 15 (Broadway), Route 222 
(Union Street) and Stillwater Avenue. 
 Such facilities are set back at least 50 feet from the street right-of-way line.
 Access drives are so located and designed to provide free, unobstructed views of 
vehicles from the drives and from the street and adequate stopping sight distances to 
such drives are available on the street. 
o Reconstruction of mobile home parks established prior to 1971 that are located outside the 
growth area delineated in the most recently adopted Comprehensive Plan, provided that the 
reconstruction is done consistent with the requirements of § 165-121C. 
o Places of worship, provided that such site development is located on a major arterial street. 
o Cemeteries, provided that they meet the requirements for access drives in Subsection D(3)(c) 
above and conform to state statutes. 
o Large landscaping services business, provided that: 
 The property is five acres or larger in area. 
 The property is on a major arterial street. 
 Facilities, equipment, and storage areas are located at least 150 feet from the property 
line of any other parcel. 
 A stockade fence at least six feet in height must enclose any storage or parking area on 
any side not facing a building on the parcel or a street adjacent to the parcel, or, in the 
alternative, at least 50 feet of existing or planted woody vegetation creating an effective 
visual barrier must be provided between facilities, equipment, and storage areas and the 
property line of any adjacent parcel. 
o Boardinghouses that are located on a major arterial street. 
o Private schools, training facilities and recreational uses on major arterials only. 
 
CURRENT PROPERTY ZONE: Urban Residence 1 District (URD-1) - § 165-88 
• Allowed Uses 
o Attached or detached dwellings containing between one and four dwelling units. 
o Home occupations or professions (subject to the requirements of Article IV). 
o Community living arrangements, in accordance with 30-A M.R.S.A. § 4357-A, as may be 
amended. 
o Small day-care center, provided that it is operated at a dwelling by a resident or residents of the 
dwelling. 
o Accessory dwelling units, under the conditions required by § 165-31.2. 
o Minor essential service facilities, under the conditions required by § 165-80.3. 
o Hosted and non-hosted short-term rentals (subject to licensing requirements in Chapter 254). 
o Accessory uses on the same lot and customarily incidental to and subordinate to the above 
uses or to an approved conditional use under Subsection D below. 
• Conditional Uses 
o Places of worship and nursing homes meeting the requirements of § 165-9 and Article XIX, 
provided that such site developments: 
 Are located on a major arterial street. 
 Have an impervious surface ratio of no more than .30. 
o Boardinghouses that are located on a major arterial street.
PROPOSED PROPERTY ZONE: Government & Institutional Service District (G&ISD) - § 165-
97 
• Allowed Uses 
o Facilities operated by public agencies or private nonprofit organizations limited to health, 
education, social welfare and cultural uses, but excluding chemical dependency treatment 
facilities. 
o Places of worship. 
o Day-care center (small or large). 
o Cemeteries. 
o Hospital complex when located on a major arterial street. 
o Nursing home. 
o Sports arenas and stadiums. 
o Chemical dependency treatment facility, provided it is located on a major arterial street and has 
a curb cut on said arterial street which provides the primary point of vehicular access for the 
facility.  
o Radio and television broadcast towers, provided that: 
 They do not exceed 195 feet in height, or the minimum height required under federal 
law, whichever is greater. 
 They are set back from all property lines a minimum of 100% of the tower height. 
 They are accessory to a public nonprofit use. 
 They conform to the requirements of § 165-80.1. 
o Minor essential service facilities, under the conditions required by § 165-80.3. 
o Accessory uses on the same lot and customarily incidental to and subordinate to the above 
uses and to a use approved under subsection below. 
• Conditional Uses 
o Medical office or clinic when: 
 Located in association with a hospital complex and on the same site; or 
 Located on a major arterial street. 
o Major essential service facilities, provided that: 
 Such facilities are not sited so as to create an extreme juxtaposition of the architectural 
scale or style to the detriment of existing buildings on adjacent lots. 
 Such uses must be certified as necessary in the particular location to service the area 
and the community. 
 That a Buffer Yard B be established for front, side and rear yards  
o Transitional housing, permanent supportive housing.  
o Secure Level IV residential care facility, provided that: 
 The facility is located on the same parcel as an existing facility owned or operated by or 
on behalf of the state that provides residential care. 
 The parcel upon which the facility is located is on a major arterial street. 
o Emergency shelters, provided that: 
 The parcel on which the facility is located is at least 100 feet from any parcel in a 
residential zone. 
 The facility shall provide adequate space for conducting security searches and other 
assessments.
 The facility shall be designed with a centralized shelter operations office on each level 
providing sight lines to sleeping areas. 
 The facility shall be designed to provide adequate indoor space to permit all shelter 
guests day shelter. 
 A management plan adequately outlining the following areas shall be provided; 
management responsibilities; process for resolving neighborhood concerns; staffing; 
access restrictions; on-site surveillance; safety measures; controls for resident behavior 
and noise levels; and monitoring reports. 
 The facility shall submit a transportation plan that identifies how the transportation needs 
of guests will be fulfilled. 
 The facility shall provide on-site services to support residents, such as case 
management, life skills training, counseling, employment and educational services, 
housing assistance, or other programs. 
 Suitable laundry, kitchen, pantry, bicycle storage, and secure storage facilities for shelter 
stayers shall be provided on-site. 
 An outdoor area for guest use shall be provided on-site with adequate screening to 
protect privacy of guests. 
 The facility shall be eligible to participate in the Maine Housing Emergency Shelter and 
Housing Assistance Program (ESHAP).
